notes.text:
The indispensable external existence premise is Darvas–Di Nezza–Lu, “Log-concavity of volume and complex Monge–Ampère equations with prescribed singularity,” arXiv:1807.00276v3, dated 12 March 2020, Theorem A(i). Its hypotheses are: a compact connected Kähler manifold, a smooth closed real (1,1)-form representing a big class, a reference of model type with positive non-pluripolar mass, and a nonnegative L^p density for some p>1 whose integral equals that mass. Its conclusion gives a solution having bounded difference from the reference, unique up to a constant. This is stronger than existence merely in a relative full-mass class. The general-measure portion of Theorem 4.7 has the latter weaker conclusion; below we use the L^p statement.

The full extracted primary article was retrieved and inspected through the immutable public mirror https://github.com/ZibangNie/SLAC-test/blob/7df78733c02ed34a285b869dafceced1bce1a4b4/data/A_structure/papers/arxiv_1807.00276.txt . The canonical primary identifier is https://arxiv.org/abs/1807.00276v3 . Direct arXiv access failed with “URLError <urlopen error [Errno 1] Operation not permitted>.” Thus the source check is of a mirrored extraction of the primary article; an official PDF was not independently authenticated. The extraction contains damaged mathematical typography, but the existence hypotheses and bounded-singularity conclusion are explicit in both Theorem A and the L^p clause of Theorem 4.7. No result below relies on an unread theorem about varying references.

Section 7 was also inspected: the convex support-function construction, Alexandrov subgradient measure, real/complex correspondence (27)–(29), and Theorem 7.2(i). The following notes independently reconstruct the model envelope and normalization constants. Section 2, construction (6), explicitly records that the non-pluripolar product gives no mass to pluripolar sets.

The operator conversion is exact. The paper displays D=i∂bar∂, whereas the question uses dd^c=D/(2π). Replace the background θ by 2πθ, leave potentials and obstacles unchanged, and multiply the target measure by (2π)^n. The genuine psh cones, envelope constructions, and bounded-difference types then coincide. Positive scaling preserves bigness. On our compact Kähler X, a fixed smooth positive dV has a smooth bounded positive ratio to an auxiliary Kähler volume ω_X^n. Consequently the bounded logarithmic densities used below give L^p densities for every finite p. Their mass normalization is verified before applying the theorem.

The foundational local ingredients are the locally bounded Bedford–Taylor products specified by the question, their continuity under locally uniform psh convergence, and removable extension of locally upper bounded psh functions across analytic subsets. The continuity needed here can be reconstructed by telescoping products: against a compactly supported smooth test, the difference of nth products is a sum of integrals of the potential difference against dd^c of the test and mixed (n−1)th products. Their local masses are bounded by repeated integration by parts with nested cutoffs and locally uniform bounds on the potentials. Uniform convergence therefore makes those integrals tend to zero. No global continuity assertion for changing singularity types is assumed.

notes.summary: Proves an explicit Hausdorff-convex-body criterion on CP^n and a fixed point blowup: a common translated simplex gives ordinary-model admissibility, limiting solvability, uniform B convergence, and exact singleton supports.
notes.detailedSummary: For θ_j=r_jπ^*ω_FS, r_j→r>0, bodies P_j⊂Σ containing a common p_*+δΣ and converging in Hausdorff distance define canonical ordinary references through restricted entropy Legendre transforms. An explicit logarithmic εθ_j-psh witness, ε=1−δ, proves the smaller-background envelope at every datum and at the limit. The reference mass is r_j^n n!Vol(P_j), giving B_j(F)=log mass_j−log∫e^F dV by the checked existence theorem. Uniform functional error is bounded by n|log(r_j/r)|+n log(1+h_j/s), s=δ/(n+√n). References converge in L^1 and locally uniformly over the torus. Every supporting set is exactly {e^F dV/∫e^F dV}; uniformly changing tests give total-variation convergence. Scope is closed projective backgrounds and one fixed blowup.
notes.text:
Scoped theorem. Let n≥2, Σ={p∈R^n:p_i≥0, ∑p_i≤1}, and ω_FS=dd^c log(1+∑|z_i|²) on CP^n, with the operator of the question. Its top integral is 1. Take X=CP^n with π the identity, or X=Bl_q CP^n for one fixed point q with π the blowdown. Put Θ=π^*ω_FS and fix any smooth positive probability volume dV on X.

Assume compact convex bodies P_j,P⊂Σ contain a common p_*+δΣ, 0<δ<1, and have Euclidean Hausdorff distances h_j=d_H(P_j,P)→0. Assume r_j>0 and r_j→r>0. Set θ_j=r_jΘ and θ=rΘ. These are geometric hypotheses; functional convergence is not assumed.

On T=(C^*)^n⊂CP^n set x_i=log|z_i|², L(x)=log(1+∑e^{x_i}), and ℓ(p)=∑p_i log p_i+(1−∑p_i)log(1−∑p_i), with 0log0=0. For K⊂Σ define h_K(x)=sup_{p∈K}p·x and g_K(x)=sup_{p∈K}(p·x−ℓ(p)). Let ψ_K and Φ_K be the genuine canonical extensions of h_K−L and g_K−L. Define φ_j=r_jπ^*Φ_{P_j} and φ=rπ^*Φ_P.

Every background is smooth closed semipositive and big. Every reference is an ordinary model with supremum zero and has a genuine smaller-background envelope with the same ε=1−δ. This includes the limiting datum. For every bounded Borel F, writing Z(F)=∫e^F dV, the scalar and functional are
c_j(F)=r_j^n n!Vol(P_j)/Z(F),
B_j(F)=log(r_j^n n!Vol(P_j))−log Z(F),
and the corresponding limiting formulas hold with r,P. If s=δ/(n+√n), then
sup_{G∈C(X)}|B_j(G)−B(G)|
=|log(r_j^n Vol(P_j)/(r^n Vol(P)))|
≤n|log(r_j/r)|+n log(1+h_j/s).
Moreover n!Vol(P_j),n!Vol(P)≥δ^n.

The backgrounds converge smoothly. The references converge in L^1(X,dV) and locally uniformly on π^{-1}(T). For continuous F,
A_j(F)=A(F)={ν_F}, where ν_F=e^F dV/Z(F).
Thus every weak cluster of supports is correctly identified. If F_j→F uniformly and ν_j∈A_j(F_j), then ν_j→ν_F in total variation, with
∫|dν_j/dV−dν_F/dV|dV≤e^{2||F_j−F||∞}−1.

Proof of extension and normalization. Convex conjugation of L gives ℓ on Σ and +∞ outside it. In its interior the maximizing relation is e^{x_i}=p_i/(1−∑p_i), and boundary values follow by limits. Since −log(n+1)≤ℓ≤0,
h_K≤g_K≤h_K+log(n+1), and g_K≤L.
Also h_K≤h_Σ=max(0,x_1,…,x_n)≤L. Convex functions of log|z_i|² are psh on T, by their Hessians and convolution. Adding local smooth projective background potentials gives locally upper bounded psh functions at the coordinate boundary. Removable extension therefore gives genuine canonical ω_FS-psh representatives. The displayed inequalities extend canonically, proving Φ_K∼ψ_K including common poles. Choose an interior p∈K, necessarily in intΣ, and x with ∇L(x)=p. Fenchel equality gives g_K(x)=L(x); hence sup Φ_K=0.

Proof of the exact model property. Let v be any genuine ω_FS-psh potential with v≤0 and v≤ψ_K+C. Supremizing its coordinate rotations and canonically regularizing gives an invariant v^T≥v with the same bounds. Upper envelopes are locally bounded above, so this regularization is psh, and upper semicontinuity of the obstacles preserves the bounds. The invariant local potential f=v^T+L is finite convex on R^n. It satisfies f≤L and f≤h_K+C. Separation implies dom f^*⊂K; the former inequality gives f^*≥ℓ. Thus Fenchel biconjugation yields
f(x)=sup_{p∈dom f^*}(p·x−f^*(p))≤g_K(x).
Every candidate is consequently ≤Φ_K. Conversely Φ_K≤0 and Φ_K≤ψ_K+log(n+1), so it is itself a candidate for the finite obstacle min(ψ_K+log(n+1),0). Therefore P_{ω_FS}[ψ_K]=Φ_K. Bounded-equivalent obstacles give the same limiting envelope because their finite-C families interlace after shifting C. It follows that P_{ω_FS}[Φ_K]=Φ_K. Positive scaling of backgrounds and obstacles commutes with these envelopes.

Proof of genuine admissibility. The inclusion p_*+δΣ⊂K⊂Σ implies p_{*,i}≥0 and b=∑p_{*,i}≤ε=1−δ. Set χ=p_*·x−εL on T. It canonically extends as an εω_FS-psh potential, with current
εω_FS+dd^cχ=∑p_{*,i}[Z_i=0]+(ε−b)[Z_0=0]≥0.
Since h_K≥p_*·x+δh_Σ and 0≤L−h_Σ≤log(n+1),
Φ_K≥h_K−L≥χ−δlog(n+1).
This is an actual genuine smaller-background candidate below Φ_K. The envelope is nonempty, bounded above by Φ_K≤0, and its regularization is genuine. Scaling and pullback give the same witnesses for all approximating and limiting references. No equation is used to infer admissibility.

Proof of the blowup assertions. A π^*ω_FS-psh potential descends. Off the exceptional divisor it defines a psh local potential downstairs. It is upper bounded near q because its pullback is upper bounded near the compact exceptional fiber. Its canonical removable extension at q is psh. Pullback agrees with the original canonical representative off the exceptional divisor and hence everywhere. Conversely genuine potentials pull back. This bijection preserves obstacles and inequalities, and therefore commutes with envelopes.

The background Θ is explicitly big. Choose unitary coordinates with q=[1:0:…:0], let ψ_q=log(∑_{i=1}^n|Z_i|²)−log(∑_{i=0}^n|Z_i|²), and let Q:Bl_q CP^n→CP^{n−1} be the resolved projection. For 0<t<1,
Θ+dd^c(tπ^*ψ_q)=(1−t)π^*ω_FS+tQ^*ω_FS,n−1+t[E_q].
The smooth sum is Kähler because (π,Q) is the graph embedding into the product and both coefficients are positive. This supplies a Kähler current in Θ and also an auxiliary Kähler form on X.

Proof of mass, including constants. For a finite convex g, let M_g be its Alexandrov measure, defined using Euclidean volume of subgradient images. With z_i=e^{x_i/2+iϑ_i}, 0≤ϑ_i<2π, one has d^cg=(1/(2π))∑g_i dϑ_i. For smooth g, angular integration gives
∫_T(dd^cg)^n=n!∫_{R^n}det(D²g)dx.
Convolution, locally uniform Bedford–Taylor continuity, and the Alexandrov formulation extend this measure identity to convex g. These are the local correspondence reconstructed above and recorded in the primary article checked in n1. In particular the total mass is n!M_g(R^n); the angular integral cancels (2π)^n.

For g=g_K every subgradient lies in K, since g≤h_K+log(n+1) and a separating direction would contradict this bound. Conversely, if p∈intK and p+cB⊂K, then g(x)−p·x≥c|x|. This function attains a minimum, so p is a subgradient somewhere. Therefore intK⊂∂g(R^n)⊂K. A convex body's boundary has zero Euclidean volume, giving M_g(R^n)=Vol(K). Non-pluripolar products give the analytic complement of T zero mass, so the actual ordinary reference has mass n!Vol(K). Pullback preserves it: outside the exceptional divisor the map is biholomorphic, and neither product charges the exceptional divisor or its image. Scaling gives r^n. This computes the reference directly and does not assume invariance under arbitrary bounded perturbations.

Proof of limiting solvability and scalar identification. The common simplex lies in the limiting P, whose computed mass m=r^n n!Vol(P)>0. Its background is smooth closed and big on compact Kähler X; its reference is ordinary model with an explicit smaller-background witness. For bounded F, the measure m e^F dV/Z(F) has mass exactly m and bounded density relative to an auxiliary Kähler volume. Apply the precise primary existence theorem audited in n1, with its specified operator conversion. It produces u∼φ solving this equation. This proves limiting solvability before asserting its functional. Apply the same argument to every approximating datum. Scalar uniqueness supplied by the question identifies the constructed constants with c_j(F) and c(F). Solutions may be normalized by sup u=0. No convergence of solution potentials is required.

Proof of geometric estimate. The common simplex has an inscribed Euclidean ball B(c,s), s=δ/(n+√n). Hausdorff distance gives P_j⊂P+h_jB. Since sB⊂P−c, convexity gives P+h_jB⊂c+(1+h_j/s)(P−c). Reversing P and P_j bounds both volume ratios by (1+h_j/s)^n. Taking logarithms and including the scale factors proves the stated uniform estimate. The simplex volume δ^n/n! supplies the positive mass lower bound.

Proof of reference topology. Let ω_ℓ(h) be the uniform-continuity modulus of ℓ on Σ. Matching maximizing points through Hausdorff distance gives
|g_{P_j}(x)−g_P(x)|≤h_j|x|+ω_ℓ(h_j).
This proves local uniform convergence over T and after pullback. The common bound χ−δlog(n+1)≤Φ_{P_j}≤0 provides an integrable logarithmic lower bound, also after pullback. Boundedness of r_j and dominated convergence off the analytic coordinate boundary give L^1(X,dV) convergence.

Proof of all support identities. Jensen gives
log Z(G)−log Z(F)=log∫e^{G−F}dν_F≥∫(G−F)dν_F,
so ν_F supports B at F. For any other support ν, put G=F+th for arbitrary continuous real h and both signs of t. Differentiating the bounded exponential integral at zero gives ∫h dν=∫h dν_F; hence ν=ν_F. If ||F_j−F||∞≤η, the density ratio lies between e^{−2η} and e^{2η}, giving the stated L^1 density estimate. Cluster identification is explicit rather than a consequence merely of compactness. No weighted non-pluripolar adjoint product is asserted.

This proof is relative to the exact external equation-existence premise in n1 and the foundational product convention of the question. Its boundary is closed projective backgrounds of this form, one fixed blowup, and convex-body references. It does not cover arbitrary nonclosed Hermitian backgrounds, moving resolutions, or unrestricted singularities. The full artifact is n2_convex_body_theorem.md; explicit families completing the criterion are in n3.

notes.text:
This note supplies actual nontrivial families for n2, including genuinely nonanalytic isolated poles and smooth residual forms that lose rank while retaining positive mass. Together with n1 and n2 it claims a complete scoped resolution of the requested geometric sufficient condition, limiting solvability, functional convergence, and support-cluster requirements. It does not claim unrestricted S08 is solved.

First family. For n≥2 and 0<a≤1 put
P_a={p_i≥0, ∑p_i≤1, ∑sqrt(p_i)≥sqrt(a)}.
The square-root sum is concave, so its superlevel set is convex. These are compact bodies containing every e_i. To exhibit a common simplex, put b=(n+1)/(2n), p_{*,i}=b/n, and δ=(n−1)/(4n). Then b+δ<1 and ∑sqrt(p_{*,i})=sqrt((n+1)/2)>1. Addition of any point of δΣ increases the square-root sum. Thus p_*+δΣ lies in every P_a, including P_1. The common smaller-background witness and limiting admissibility follow from n2 with ε=1−δ.

The reference is the explicit ordinary model Φ_{P_a} from n2. Its prototype ψ_{P_a} has exactly one pole, p=[1:0:…:0]. Since e_i∈P_a,
ψ_{P_a}≥log(max_{1≤i≤n}|Z_i|²)−log(∑_{i=0}^n|Z_i|²),
which is locally bounded below away from p. At p, Cauchy–Schwarz gives ∑p_i≥a/n for every point of P_a. When all x_i=log|z_i|² are negative,
h_{P_a}(x)≤(a/n)max_i x_i→−∞.
The bounded equivalence of Φ and ψ proves the same canonical pole locus. On a blowup at q≠p it remains a single point π^{-1}(p); the reference is bounded near the other exceptional divisor. Every generic divisorial Lelong number is zero, yet the reference is unbounded. These types are nondivisorial.

They are genuinely nonanalytic types. For λ_i>0, examine |z_i|²=e^{−Rλ_i}. Minimizing ∑λ_i p_i over P_a and writing y_i=sqrt(p_i), Cauchy–Schwarz gives
 y_i=sqrt(a)/(λ_i∑_kλ_k^{-1}),
 min ∑λ_i p_i=a/(∑_iλ_i^{-1}).
The minimizer satisfies ∑p_i≤a≤1, so the simplex constraint is respected. Since L(−Rλ)→0 and Φ−ψ is bounded, the directional logarithmic coefficient is
 d_a(λ)=a/(∑_iλ_i^{-1}).

Suppose this type were bounded-equivalent to c log(∑_{k=1}^N|f_k|²)+O(1), with holomorphic germs f_k. Average ∑|f_k|² over coordinate phases. Taylor orthogonality makes the average ∑_{k,α}|c_{k,α}|²e^{−Rα·λ}. Bounded equivalence to the invariant reference forces its exponential rate to be d_a(λ)/c. The rate of this convergent nonnegative series is the minimum weighted monomial degree α·λ among nonzero coefficients. On a compact neighborhood of a strictly positive λ, only finitely many monomials can minimize: a positive lower bound on each λ_i and comparison with one fixed nonzero coefficient bound their total degrees. Hence every analytic type has a locally piecewise linear directional coefficient. On λ=(s,1,…,1), however,
 d_a(λ)=a s/(1+(n−1)s),
whose second derivative is −2a(n−1)/(1+(n−1)s)^3<0 on every open interval. This is incompatible with finite piecewise linearity. Smooth remainders and bounded changes do not alter the coefficients. Thus the references are not bounded-equivalent to analytic singularities.

The removed corner C_a={p_i≥0:∑sqrt(p_i)<sqrt(a)} equals aC_1 and lies in Σ. Substitution p_i=y_i² gives
 Vol(C_1)=2^n∫_{y_i≥0,∑y_i<1}∏y_i dy=2^n/(2n)!.
The integral follows by iterated monomial integration on a simplex. Therefore
 n!Vol(P_a)=1−κ_n a^n,
 κ_n=2^n n!/(2n)!=1/(2n−1)!!<1.
For θ_r=rΘ and φ_{r,a}=rπ^*Φ_{P_a}, n2 now gives
 B_{r,a}(F)=n log r+log(1−κ_n a^n)−log∫e^F dV,
 A_{r,a}(F)={e^F dV/∫e^F dV}.
In particular the limiting a=1 type has positive mass r^n(1−κ_n) and is an explicitly admissible, solvable ordinary model class.

A concrete family is a_j=1−1/(j+2), r_j=1+1/(j+2), j≥1, tending to a=r=1. Its backgrounds converge smoothly and references converge in the topologies proved in n2. Moreover d_H(P_{a_j},P_1)≤1−a_j. Indeed for p∈P_{a_j}\P_1 put u=(∑sqrt(p_i))²∈[a_j,1); then p/u∈P_1. As |p|≤∑p_i≤u, the distance is at most 1−u≤1−a_j. Uniformly over all continuous G,
 sup_G|B_{r_j,a_j}(G)−B_{1,1}(G)|
 =|n log r_j+log((1−κ_n a_j^n)/(1−κ_n))|

For a locally uniformly upper-bounded family of plurisubharmonic functions on a domain, the upper semicontinuous regularization of their supremum is plurisubharmonic and equals that supremum almost everywhere (Demailly I.5.7).
A plurisubharmonic function off a closed pluripolar subset of a complex manifold, locally bounded above near that subset, has a unique plurisubharmonic extension (Demailly I.5.24).

Locally bounded plurisubharmonic functions have closed positive mixed Bedford–Taylor products; locally uniform convergence to finite continuous plurisubharmonic limits implies weak convergence of these products (Demailly III.3.2 and III.3.6).
For a holomorphic function f not identically zero on any component, log|f|² is locally integrable and (i/(2π))∂bar∂log|f|² is its zero-divisor current, counting multiplicities (Demailly III.2.15).

For a compact convex body K⊂R^n_{≥0}, nontrivial rotation-invariant plurisubharmonic functions U on (C*)^n satisfying U≤h_K(Log)+C are exactly U=g(Log) with g finite convex and g≤h_K+C, where Log_i=log|z_i|² (DDL equation (27), with logarithmic coordinates rescaled).
For finite convex g:R^n→R, M_g(E)=Vol(∂g(E)) defines its Borel Alexandrov measure. For U(z)=g(log|z_1|²,…,log|z_n|²) and dd^c=i∂bar∂/(2π), Log_*((dd^cU)^n)=n!M_g (Berman–Berndtsson §§2.1–2.2).
For finite convex functions f,h on R^n, Legendre–Fenchel conjugation satisfies f**=f and f≤h if and only if f*≥h* (Berman–Berndtsson §2.3).

On a compact Kähler manifold, non-pluripolar products of closed positive (1,1)-currents are finite closed positive currents, local in the plurifine topology, and their trace measures charge no pluripolar sets (BEGZ §1.2, Proposition 1.6 and Theorem 1.8).

For the blowup of a smooth complex n-fold at a point, the exceptional divisor is CP^{n−1}, local coordinates satisfy z_j=w_j and z_k=w_jw_k for k≠j, and its normal bundle is O_CP^{n−1}(−1) (Demailly VII.12.2–12.4).

On a compact Kähler manifold, if T is a closed positive current of bidimension (1,1) and u,v are bounded quasi-plurisubharmonic functions, then ∫_X u dd^cv∧T=∫_X v dd^cu∧T, with the integrals defined in the Bedford–Taylor sense (BEGZ Theorem 1.14 with A=∅).

notes.detailedSummary: Convex duality proves that every truncated model envelope equals Phi_K. A translated delta simplex provides an explicit smaller-background logarithmic competitor and a common integrable lower bound. The toric Monge–Ampère formula gives actual mass r^n n!Vol(K), and the granted existence theorem applies separately to every reference and the limit. The common inscribed ball yields the exact logarithmic volume bound. The scalar formula identifies all supporting probabilities and proves total variation convergence. Independent retrieval of the foundational source texts was unavailable; their supplied statements are treated as premises.
notes.text:
All products below are the non-pluripolar Monge–Ampère products in the stated closed projective setting, with dd^c=i∂bar∂/(2π), and all representatives are canonical. This is an analytic proof under the explicitly granted foundational premises, not a numerical result.

1. Entropy and canonical extensions.

Write w_0=1−∑p_i and w_i=p_i. Then ℓ(p)=∑_{i=0}^n w_i log w_i is continuous and strictly convex on Σ, and −log(n+1)≤ℓ≤0. The lower bound follows from nonnegativity of relative entropy against the uniform probability; the upper bound follows from w_i≤1. Nonnegativity of relative entropy follows directly from log t≤t−1, including zero weights by continuity.

For v_0=1/(1+∑e^{x_i}), v_i=e^{x_i}/(1+∑e^{x_i}), the entropy identity gives
L(x)=max_{p∈Σ}(p·x−ℓ(p)),
with maximizer p_i=v_i. Consequently L*=ℓ on Σ and L*=+∞ off Σ. At a boundary point, approximate its probability weights by mixtures with the uniform distribution and choose x_i=log(v_i/v_0); the relative entropy tends to zero, proving the boundary conjugate identity. Outside Σ, separation and L(ty)≤t h_Σ(y)+log(n+1) prove that the conjugate is infinite.

For a compact convex body K⊂Σ,
h_K≤g_K≤h_K+log(n+1), and h_K≤L, g_K≤L.                                      (1)

These are finite convex functions. By supplied premise 5, h_K∘ℒ and g_K∘ℒ are locally bounded psh on T. In the chart Z_k≠0, a local potential for h_K−L is h_K(x)−log|Z_k/Z_0|², and similarly for g_K. The subtracted term is pluriharmonic on T, and (1) bounds these potentials above by the smooth local Fubini–Study potential log(∑|Z_i|²/|Z_k|²). The chart complement of T is closed analytic and pluripolar. Supplied premise 2 gives unique canonical psh extensions. They agree on overlaps by uniqueness, with the usual pluriharmonic transition functions. Thus ψ_K and Φ_K exist as genuine global ω_FS-psh functions, finite on T.

Taking canonical limits in (1) gives globally
ψ_K≤Φ_K≤ψ_K+log(n+1).                                                         (2)
Their pole sets coincide, and both canonical values are −∞ at every common pole. This is the claimed bounded ordinary equivalence; no subtraction of infinities is intended. Analytic sets here are locally pluripolar by logarithms of nonzero holomorphic defining functions.

2. Exact ordinary model property.

Φ_K≤0. A convex body has nonempty Euclidean interior, so choose p∈int K⊂int Σ. At x_i=log(p_i/(1−∑p_i)), p is the unrestricted entropy maximizer and lies in K. Therefore g_K(x)=L(x), and sup Φ_K=0.

For C≥0 let v_C=P_{ω_FS}(min(Φ_K+C,0)). The family is nonempty because Φ_K is a competitor. Local potentials are uniformly bounded above by the local Fubini–Study potential, so premise 3 makes the regularized envelope psh. Its canonical value remains below the upper semicontinuous obstacle. Torus rotations preserve the background and obstacle, hence v_C is rotation invariant. On T, Φ_K≤v_C≤0, so it is finite there.

A finite rotation-invariant psh potential on T is convex in x: on the exponential covering w↦(e^{w_1/2},…,e^{w_n/2}), its pullback is f(Re w); subharmonicity on complex lines in real directions gives nonnegative distributional directional second derivatives. Local convolution and passage to the canonical representative give convexity. Thus f_C=L+v_C is finite convex and satisfies
f_C≤L,   f_C≤g_K+C.                                                           (3)

The conjugate g_K* is infinite outside K. Indeed, for p∉K choose y with p·y>h_K(y). Then
p·ty−g_K(ty)≥t(p·y−h_K(y))−log(n+1)→+∞.
By (3) and premise 7, f_C*≥L*, and f_C*≥g_K*−C. Hence f_C* is infinite outside K and at least ℓ on K. Finite-convex biconjugacy gives
f_C(x)=f_C**(x)≤sup_{p∈K}(p·x−ℓ(p))=g_K(x).
The competitor Φ_K gives the opposite inequality. Thus v_C=Φ_K on T and globally by canonical uniqueness. Every C≥0 truncated envelope already equals Φ_K, proving P_{ω_FS}[Φ_K]=Φ_K exactly.

3. Descent through an arbitrary-point blowup; background geometry.

For π:X=Bl_q CP^n→CP^n, every canonical π*ω_FS-psh function u descends. It is bounded above on compact X. Define v=u∘π^{-1} outside q. After adding a smooth local background potential, v is psh and bounded above near q, so premise 2 extends it canonically across q. Its pullback is π*ω_FS-psh and agrees with u outside the exceptional divisor. Applying the same canonical uniqueness in blowup charts gives u=π*v everywhere. Pullback of local psh potentials is psh by composition with a holomorphic map; it is not identically −∞ because it is finite on a dense open set. This proves the same descent for any positive multiple of the background.

Therefore envelopes with pulled-back obstacles are pullbacks of downstairs envelopes. Inequalities are first checked off the exceptional divisor and then extended canonically. For r>0,
P_{rΘ}(min(rπ*Φ_K+C,0))=rπ*P_{ω_FS}(min(Φ_K+C/r,0))=rπ*Φ_K.
The supremum is zero, so every scaled pullback reference is an ordinary model. No toric condition on q is required.

For completeness, the blowup is Kähler and Θ is big by an explicit construction. A unitary coordinate change takes q to [1:0:…:0] and preserves ω_FS. The blowup is the smooth incidence variety in CP^n×CP^{n−1} defined by Z_iW_j=Z_jW_i, i,j≥1. Its maps are π and the resolved direction map Q_q. Near the exceptional divisor its charts are Z=(1,s,sw_2,…,sw_n), W=(1,w_2,…,w_n). Thus (π,Q_q) is an immersion, including s=0; elsewhere π is locally biholomorphic. Consequently
β_η=(1−η)π*ω_FS+ηQ_q*ω_FS,n−1
is Kähler for 0<η<1: the differential kernels of its two summands intersect trivially.

For the homogeneous prototype
χ_η=η[log(∑_{i=1}^n|Z_i|²)−log(∑_{i=0}^n|Z_i|²)],
the local identity log(∑_{i=1}^n|Z_i|²)∘π=log|s|²+log(1+∑_{i=2}^n|w_i|²), together with premise 8, gives
Θ+dd^c(χ_η∘π)=β_η+η[E_q].                                                     (4)
This current represents [Θ] and dominates a Kähler form, proving bigness by definition. Θ is smooth, closed, and semipositive; its positive multiples are likewise big. For CP^n, ω_FS is already Kähler. Both manifolds are compact and connected.

4. Smaller-background envelope with exactly epsilon=1-delta.

Suppose p_*+δΣ⊂K. Then p_{*,i}≥0 and ∑p_{*,i}≤1−δ. Put ε=1−δ and define on T
v=p_*·x−εL−δlog(n+1).
Since p_*∈εΣ, the chart extension argument gives a genuine canonical εω_FS-psh function. Explicitly its homogeneous expression is
∑_{i=1}^n p_{*,i}log|Z_i|²+(ε−∑p_{*,i})log|Z_0|²−εlog(∑|Z_i|²)−δlog(n+1).
All logarithmic coefficients are nonnegative, and v≤0. The translated simplex gives h_K≥p_*·x+δh_Σ, while h_Σ≥L−log(n+1). Hence
v≤h_K−L=ψ_K≤Φ_K
canonically everywhere. Thus rπ*v is a genuine εrΘ-psh competitor in P_{εrΘ}(rπ*Φ_K). The family is bounded above by the upper semicontinuous obstacle and nonempty; premise 3 yields a genuine envelope, not identically −∞. This proves admissibility with ε=1−δ for all members and the limit.

5. Actual mass and independently obtained solutions.

Strict convexity of ℓ makes the maximizer p(x) of p·x−ℓ(p) over K unique. Difference quotients of this maximum over a compact set show ∂g_K(x)={p(x)}: nearby maximizers have limit points among the maximizers at x. Thus every subgradient belongs to K. Conversely every p∈int K belongs to int Σ and, at x=∇ℓ(p), is the unrestricted and restricted maximizer. Therefore
int K⊂∪_x∂g_K(x)⊂K,   M_{g_K}(R^n)=Vol_n(K).
By premise 5, the total torus mass of (dd^c(g_K∘ℒ))^n is n!Vol(K). By premise 6 this is the non-pluripolar product of the canonical reference current on T, and the analytic complement has zero non-pluripolar mass. Hence its actual mass is n!Vol(K).

On a blowup, currents and products correspond under the biholomorphism away from the center and exceptional divisor; all omitted analytic sets, including the center if it lies in T, have zero non-pluripolar mass. Positive scaling gives
m_j=r_j^n n!Vol(P_j),   m=r^n n!Vol(P).
The common simplex gives n!Vol(P_j),n!Vol(P)≥δ^n>0.

Fix a Kähler form Ω on X. For bounded real Borel F, Z(F)=∫e^F dV is finite and positive. For reference mass m_K set
f=(m_K/Z(F))e^F(dV/Ω^n).
The volume ratio is smooth and bounded on compact X, so f≥0 belongs to every finite L^p, p>1, and ∫fΩ^n=m_K. X is compact connected Kähler; the background is smooth closed and big; the reference is an exact ordinary model of positive mass. These verify every hypothesis of supplied premise 1, Darvas–Di Nezza–Lu Theorem A(i). It supplies an ordinary-type solution with measure (m_K/Z(F))e^F dV. Apply it separately to every j and to the limit. No limiting solution is assumed.

The source convention uses i∂bar∂. Literally apply it with source background 2πθ and source Kähler form 2πΩ, keeping the potential unchanged. Its current and mass are respectively 2π and (2π)^n times ours. The source density relative to (2πΩ)^n is the same f above, and its total integral is (2π)^n m_K. Dividing its equation by (2π)^n yields exactly our equation and the same model-envelope convention.

Granted scalar uniqueness applies because section 4 proved admissibility. Thus
c_j(F)=m_j/Z(F),   c(F)=m/Z(F),
B_j(F)=log m_j−log Z(F),   B(F)=log m−log Z(F).                                 (5)

6. Reference convergence and the exact geometric estimate.

Let ω_ℓ denote the uniform continuity modulus of ℓ on Σ. Hausdorff approximation in both directions gives
|g_{P_j}(x)−g_P(x)|≤h_j|x|+ω_ℓ(h_j).
Thus the references converge locally uniformly on T. They also converge locally uniformly on π^{-1}(T): any compact subset has compact image in T, and the continuous downstairs representatives pull back by literal composition, even when q∈T. Scaling by r_j→r preserves this convergence. The backgrounds converge in C^∞ because θ_j−θ=(r_j−r)Θ.

The v in section 4 is a common nonpositive lower bound. Its pullback is integrable against smooth dV. Indeed, each logarithm in its homogeneous expression is a projective hyperplane-section logarithm. A hyperplane through q pulls back to its smooth strict transform plus the exceptional divisor; in blowup charts its individual defining function is a unit times a coordinate or the product of the exceptional coordinate with a transverse coordinate. A hyperplane not through q has no exceptional factor. Consequently these logarithms are locally sums of log|coordinate|² and smooth terms, integrable because ∫_0^a r|log r|dr<∞. A finite chart cover proves global integrability.

Choose R≥sup_j r_j and R≥r. Then Rπ*v≤φ_j,φ≤0. Local uniform convergence gives pointwise convergence outside an analytic set of smooth volume zero. Dominated convergence proves φ_j→φ in L^1(X,dV).

Set s=δ/(n+√n) and c_0=p_*+(s,…,s). The ball B((s,…,s),s) lies in δΣ: the distances to coordinate faces are s, and the distance to ∑p_i=δ is (δ−ns)/√n=s. Thus every body contains B(c_0,s). Hausdorff inclusions and convexity imply
P_j⊂P+h_j B⊂c_0+(1+h_j/s)(P−c_0),
P⊂P_j+h_j B⊂c_0+(1+h_j/s)(P_j−c_0).
Here h_jB⊂(h_j/s)(P−c_0), and A+tA=(1+t)A for convex A. Taking volumes in both directions gives
|log(Vol(P_j)/Vol(P))|≤n log(1+h_j/s).
In particular volumes and masses converge, with positive limit. From (5), the functional difference is constant in G, so
sup_{G continuous}|B_j(G)−B(G)|
=|log(r_j^n Vol(P_j)/(r^n Vol(P)))|
≤n|log(r_j/r)|+n log(1+h_j/s).

7. Supporting probabilities and total variation.

Put ρ_F=e^F/Z(F). By (5), the defining supporting inequality is
log Z(G)≥log Z(F)+∫(G−F)dν   for every continuous real G.                       (6)
For ν=ρ_FdV this follows from Jensen applied to log∫e^{G−F}ρ_FdV. Conversely, for continuous F insert G=F+tH, where H is continuous, use both signs of t, and differentiate at zero under the bounded integral. This gives ∫H dν=∫Hρ_FdV for every H. Continuous functions determine measures on compact X, so ν=ρ_FdV. The mass term cancels for every j, proving
A_j(F)=A(F)={e^F dV/Z(F)}.

This remains true for bounded Borel F if that extended domain is used. For a fixed candidate ν, choose uniformly bounded continuous F_k→F almost everywhere for ν+dV. Such approximation follows from measure regularity, approximating indicators between closed and open sets by continuous functions, then simple functions, and choosing summable L^1 errors. Insert G=F_k+tH in (6), pass to the limit by dominated convergence, and use the same derivative argument. Jensen still proves sufficiency.

If η_j=||F_j−F||_∞, then e^{−η_j}≤Z(F_j)/Z(F)≤e^{η_j} and
e^{−2η_j}≤ρ_{F_j}/ρ_F≤e^{2η_j}.
Hence
∫|ρ_{F_j}−ρ_F|dV≤e^{2η_j}−1.
Every ν_j∈A_j(F_j) is this Gibbs probability, so it converges in total variation. The variation norm of the signed difference equals the displayed L^1 error; the convention sup_E|ν_j(E)−ν(E)| is half as large. Every support cluster is identified.

notes.text:
This note uses n1 for canonical extensions, ordinary models, admissibility, actual masses, solvability, convergence, and supporting probabilities. The curved-body calculations and nonanalyticity argument are proved here.

1. Convexity, common simplex, and pole set.

S(p)=∑√p_i is continuous and concave on the nonnegative orthant. Its superlevel set is closed and convex, so P_a is compact and convex. For b=(n+1)/(2n), p_{*,i}=b/n, δ=(n−1)/(4n), every point of p_*+δΣ satisfies
∑p_i≤b+δ=(3n+1)/(4n)<1,
∑√p_i≥n√(b/n)=√((n+1)/2)>1,   n≥2.
Thus this common translated simplex lies in every P_a, including P_1. It has nonempty interior and 0<δ<1. These are convex bodies, and n1 gives admissibility with ε=1−δ directly at every a.

For any projective point other than p=[1:0:…:0], some Z_i, i≥1, is nonzero. The vertex e_i belongs to P_a and ℓ(e_i)=0, hence canonically
Φ_{P_a}≥log|Z_i|²−log(∑_{k=0}^n|Z_k|²).
Together with Φ_{P_a}≤0 this proves local boundedness wherever Z_i≠0.

For every p'∈P_a, Cauchy–Schwarz gives ∑p'_i≥a/n. If x_i≤M<0, then p'·x≤(a/n)M, and therefore
g_{P_a}(x)≤(a/n)M+log(n+1).
As z→0, M=max_i log|z_i|²→−∞, including the canonical limits on coordinate hyperplanes. Hence Φ_{P_a}(p)=−∞. Its pole set is exactly {p}.

Because n≥2, every divisor has generic points away from this single point. Local boundedness implies zero Lelong number there, proving zero generic divisorial Lelong numbers. For q≠p, the reference is bounded near q, so its pullback is bounded near E_q and has exactly the single pole π^{-1}(p).

2. Directional formula and failure of analytic ordinary type.

For λ_i>0 put S_λ=∑λ_i^{-1}. Cauchy–Schwarz gives
(∑√p_i)^2≤(∑λ_i p_i)S_λ,
so min_{p∈P_a}λ·p≥a/S_λ. Equality occurs at
p_i=a/(S_λ²λ_i²).
Indeed ∑√p_i=√a and ∑p_i=a∑λ_i^{-2}/S_λ²≤a≤1. Thus
min_{p∈P_a}λ·p=a/S_λ.
Since h_{P_a}(−Rλ)=−R min λ·p, |g_{P_a}−h_{P_a}|≤log(n+1), and L(−Rλ)→0,
lim_{R→∞}−Φ_{P_a}(|z_i|²=e^{−Rλ_i})/R=d_a(λ)=a/(∑λ_i^{-1}).                  (7)

Suppose the type were c log(∑_{k=1}^N|f_k|²)+O(1), c>0, for holomorphic germs at p. At least one germ is nonzero. On an open box of positive directions with 0<u≤λ_i≤v, fix a nonzero monomial of some germ of degree D_0. The minimum monomial weight is at most vD_0. Choose D with u(D+1)>vD_0+1. Monomials of degree greater than D cannot attain that minimum. Thus only a fixed finite set of exponents matters on this box.

Remove the finitely many hyperplanes (α−β)·λ=0 between distinct relevant exponents. On some nonempty open cell the minimum exponent α is fixed and unique. Along z_i=e^{−Rλ_i/2}, its Taylor term dominates at least one germ. Other finite terms have strictly greater weight; absolute convergence on a fixed polydisc bounds the Taylor tail by a constant times e^{−Ru(D+1)/2}. Hence the squared-norm logarithmic coefficient on this cell is cα·λ. There is no cancellation assertion on the removed hyperplanes; uniqueness prevents cancellation on the cell itself.

Bounded equivalence and (7) imply d_a(λ)=cα·λ on that open cell. But with S'=∑_{i=2}^nλ_i^{-1}>0,
d_a(λ)=aλ_1/(1+S'λ_1),
∂²d_a/∂λ_1²=−2aS'/(1+S'λ_1)^3<0.
An open cell contains an interval varying λ_1 with the other coordinates fixed. This contradicts linearity. Thus the ordinary type is not equivalent to any analytic singularity of the required form. The proof also applies upstairs near the pole when q≠p, since the blowdown is biholomorphic there.

3. Exact volume and functional.

The excluded region S(p)<√a automatically satisfies ∑p_i≤S(p)^2<a≤1, so the top simplex constraint is redundant there. Substitute p_i=u_i². Its volume is
2^n∫_{u_i≥0,∑u_i<√a}∏u_i du
=2^n a^n∫_{v_i≥0,∑v_i<1}∏v_i dv
=2^n a^n/(2n)!.
The last integral is the elementary simplex identity
∫_{∑v_i≤1}∏v_i^{k_i}dv=∏k_i!/(n+∑k_i)!
for nonnegative integers k_i, applied with k_i=1. The identity follows inductively from integration by parts in ∫_0^1 s^k(1−s)^m ds=k!m!/(k+m+1)!. Boundary level sets have zero Lebesgue measure.

Therefore
n!Vol(P_a)=1−κ_n a^n,
κ_n=2^n n!/(2n)!=1/(2n−1)!!.
For n≥2, κ_n≤1/3<1. By n1, for either allowed background and every bounded Borel F, an actual ordinary-type solution exists with
c_{r,a}(F)=r^n(1−κ_n a^n)/Z(F),
B_{r,a}(F)=n log r+log(1−κ_n a^n)−log Z(F),
A_{r,a}(F)={e^F dV/Z(F)}.
At a=r=1 the same common simplex directly proves admissibility, and the existence theorem is applied independently there. Its mass is 1−κ_n>0, equal to 2/3 for n=2.

4. Hausdorff estimate and actual nonconstant types.

P_1⊂P_a. For p'∈P_a, write S=∑p'_i and d=max(a,S)∈(0,1], and put p''=p'/d. If d=a, then ∑p''_i≤1 and ∑√p''_i≥1. If d=S, its coordinates sum to 1, which also implies ∑√p''_i≥1. Thus p''∈P_1. Moreover
|p''−p'|=(1−d)|p'|/d≤(1−d)S/d≤1−a.
This proves d_H(P_a,P_1)≤1−a in Euclidean distance.

For e_j=1/(j+2), a_j=1−e_j, r_j=1+e_j, the displayed family is nonconstant and tends to a=r=1. Since

notes.text:
This note uses n1 for the general convex-body theorem, extension and model arguments. It proves the endpoint assertion directly, without assuming a general theorem of mass invariance under bounded differences. The normalization remains dd^c=i∂bar∂/(2π).

1. Prototype, common simplex, and functional estimates.

In the chart Z_0=1 put M=max_i x_i and S=∑e^{x_i}. For K_t={p∈Σ:∑p_i≥t}, allocation to a largest coordinate shows
h_{K_t}(x)=(1−t)max(0,M)+tM.
If M≥0 the optimal coordinate sum is 1; if M≤0 it is t. The prototype local potential is
f_t=L+ψ_t=(1−t)L+t log S.
Since max(0,M)≤L≤max(0,M)+log(n+1) and M≤log S≤M+log n,
h_{K_t}≤f_t≤h_{K_t}+(1−t)log(n+1)+t log n≤h_{K_t}+log(n+1).
The same interval contains g_{K_t}, by n1. Consequently
|ψ_t−Φ_{K_t}|≤log(n+1)
off their poles, with canonical agreement at common poles. The homogeneous ψ_t is ≤0, smooth away from p, and −∞ at p. Convexity of f_t and the chart extension argument give its genuine ω_FS-psh representative. The comparison persists after pullback to X.

For 0<t_min≤t≤t_max<1, take p_{*,i}=t_max/n and δ=(1−t_max)/2. Points of p_*+δΣ have nonnegative coordinates and sum between t_max and (1+t_max)/2<1. Thus the translated simplex lies in every K_t, and n1 applies with ε=1−δ, including the limit. Removing tΣ from Σ gives
n!Vol(K_t)=1−t^n,
B_{r,t}(F)=n log r+log(1−t^n)−log Z(F),
A_{r,t}(F)={e^F dV/Z(F)}.

To check the Hausdorff hypothesis, let t≤s≤t_max. The inclusion K_s⊂K_t holds. For p'∈K_t with coordinate sum A<s, move toward a fixed vertex e_i until its sum is s. The parameter is (s−A)/(1−A)≤(s−t)/(1−t_max), and the distance is at most √2 times that parameter, since diam Σ=√2. Therefore
d_H(K_s,K_t)≤√2|s−t|/(1−t_max).
Thus t_j→t implies Hausdorff convergence. The derivative bound
|d/dt log(1−t^n)|≤nt_max^{n−1}/(1−t_max^n)
gives precisely
sup_G|B_j(G)−B(G)|
≤n|log(r_j/r)|+[nt_max^{n−1}/(1−t_max^n)]|t_j−t|.

For j≥1, t_j=1/2+1/[4(j+1)] lies in [1/2,5/8], and r_j=1+1/(j+2) tends to 1. The limiting mass is 1−2^{−n}. The explicit prototype has directional coefficient t min_i λ_i; the model has the same coefficient by bounded comparison. Thus the scaled references have coefficient r_jt_j min_i λ_i. Both positive factors decrease strictly, so r_jt_j decreases strictly to 1/2. Their actual ordinary types are pairwise distinct.

2. Kähler residual and exact current identity.

Let Y=Bl_p CP^n. The direction map Q_p resolves [Z_1:…:Z_n]. Near its exceptional divisor, incidence charts are
Z=(1,s,sw_2,…,sw_n),   Q_p=(1,w_2,…,w_n).
The map (π_p,Q_p) into CP^n×CP^{n−1} is an immersion, as in n1. Thus
β_t=(1−t)π_p*ω_FS+tQ_p*ω_FS,n−1
is Kähler for 0<t<1: both terms are smooth closed semipositive, their kernels intersect trivially, and both coefficients are positive.

The centers p and q are disjoint. Blowing them up in either order gives the same manifold, since the identical local constructions in disjoint neighborhoods and their common complement glue. Thus τ:Z→X and σ:Z→Y satisfy π∘τ=π_p∘σ; E_p and E_q are disjoint. Set α_t=σ*β_t.

In the chart above,
log(∑_{i=1}^n|Z_i|²)∘π_p=log|s|²+log(1+∑_{i=2}^n|w_i|²).
Supplied Poincaré–Lelong premise 8, with multiplicity one and the problem's normalization, gives
π_p*ω_FS+dd^c(ψ_t∘π_p)=β_t+t[E_p on Y].
The center of σ is disjoint from E_p. Its pullback defining section therefore has divisor exactly E_p on Z, without an E_q factor. Equivalently the prototype is smooth near q, so pulling back there creates no logarithmic term. Hence the exact identity is
(π∘τ)*ω_FS+dd^c(ψ_t∘π∘τ)=α_t+t[E_p].                                       (8)
Local pluriharmonic transition terms ensure that these are global current identities. There is no exceptional coefficient along E_q.

3. Rank, mass, and failure of a positive lower bound.

α_t is smooth, closed, and semipositive; it is positive away from E_q, where σ is locally biholomorphic. A chart of the second blowup has
σ(s,w_2,…,w_n)=(s,sw_2,…,sw_n)
in coordinates centered at its center in Y. At s=0 its differential has image the line spanned by (1,w_2,…,w_n), and kills all tangent w-directions. It has complex rank exactly one. Pullback of a positive Hermitian form has rank equal to that differential rank. Therefore α_t has rank exactly one everywhere on E_q.

A direct toric calculation gives its top integral, without mass invariance or an intersection calculation. For 0<t<1,
(∇f_t)_i=(e^{x_i}/S)[t+(1−t)S/(1+S)].
Its coordinates are positive, and their sum A lies in (t,1). Conversely, for any point of int K_t of sum A, set S=(A−t)/(1−A) and e^{x_i}=S p_i/A. This yields that point as ∇f_t. Thus ∇f_t(R^n)=int K_t, and premise 5 gives total torus mass 1−t^n.

On π_p^{-1}(T), the current in (8) before the second pullback is exactly β_t. The complement is analytic and has zero measure for the smooth top form β_t^n. Consequently ∫_Yβ_t^n=1−t^n. Under σ, the complements of its center and exceptional divisor are biholomorphic; omitted sets have zero smooth measure. Therefore
∫_Zα_t^n=∫_Yβ_t^n=1−t^n>0.                                                   (9)

For any Kähler form Ω_Z, a nonzero tangent vector to E_q has α_t-value zero and Ω_Z-value positive. Such vectors exist because n≥2. Hence there is no c>0 with α_t≥cΩ_Z.

4. Bounded canonical residual of the ordinary model.

Off E_p define w_t=(Φ_{K_t}−ψ_t)∘π∘τ. It is bounded by section 1. In a chart meeting E_p, let s define E_p and let ρ_t be a smooth local potential of α_t. The model local potential has, up to a pluriharmonic term, the form
ρ_t+w_t+t log|s|².
Off E_p, subtracting the pluriharmonic logarithm leaves the psh function ρ_t+w_t. Its upper and lower bounds extend to the divisor by canonical extension, using premise 2. Uniqueness makes the local extensions compatible, so w_t is a bounded canonical α_t-psh function globally.

The extended functions agree with the original potentials almost everywhere. Their locally integrable distributions therefore agree after restoring t log|s|², and Poincaré–Lelong gives
(π∘τ)*ω_FS+dd^c(Φ_{K_t}∘π∘τ)=α_t+dd^c w_t+t[E_p].                           (10)
This proves exactly the residual assertion, with its finite canonical meaning at the common poles. There is no logarithmic coefficient on E_q: the prototype is smooth there and w_t is bounded. Multiplication by r gives residual rα_t, correction dd^c(rw_t), and exceptional coefficient rt.

5. Every endpoint ordinary-type potential has zero mass.

Let u∈PSH(X,Θ) satisfy u∼ψ_1∘π. By n1's descent lemma, u=π*u_0 for a canonical ω_FS-psh u_0 on CP^n. The bounded comparison with ψ_1 holds outside q and then canonically everywhere. Resolving p on Y, the same bounded-residual construction as in section 4 gives a bounded canonical Q_p*ω_FS,n−1-psh function w with
π_p*ω_FS+dd^c(u_0∘π_p)=Q_p*ω_FS,n−1+dd^c w+[E_p on Y].                        (11)

Q_p is a holomorphic CP^1 bundle: over [W] the fiber is the projective line [Z_0:sW_1:…:sW_n], with its point s=0 interpreted in the blowup. This description trivializes over standard base charts. Restricting the bounded local psh residual potential to a fiber gives a bounded subharmonic function w on compact connected CP^1, since the background restricts to zero. The maximum principle makes it constant. Thus w=v∘Q_p for a bounded function v on CP^{n−1}. Local holomorphic sections show that v is canonical ω_FS,n−1-psh.

The residual in (11) is therefore Q_p*(ω_FS,n−1+dd^c v), whose top Bedford–Taylor product in dimension n is zero. This remains valid for bounded, possibly discontinuous v. In a product chart (y,s), a local potential a(y)=ρ(y)+v(y) depends only on y∈C^{n−1}. The locally bounded Bedford–Taylor recursive definition
(dd^c a)^k=dd^c(a(dd^c a)^{k−1})
has only horizontal components independent of s at every step. At degree n the horizontal dimension n−1 forces zero, and no vertical derivative occurs. This is an identity in the recursive definition, not an assumed convergence theorem.

Outside E_p the current in (11) equals this residual. Premise 6 identifies its non-pluripolar product there and assigns the divisor zero mass. Its total mass on Y is zero. Biholomorphisms away from the centers, together with zero mass of the omitted analytic sets, give zero mass for u_0 and for u. This proves the assertion for every potential in the endpoint ordinary type.

If c>0 and bounded real F solved the equation in that type, integration would give 0=cZ(F)>0, a contradiction. The endpoint t=1 is excluded. In contrast, n2 proves explicit admissibility and independent solvability at a=1 with mass 1−κ_n>0.
